newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court strikes down systematic inspection costs on exports.
newsitem.headline: Court strikes down systematic inspection costs on exports.

text.p: The European Court of Justice precluded on Tuesday systematic on-site inspections to verify the composition of skimmed-milk powder within an exporting state, and not at the frontier.
The court said spot inspections were allowed, but distinguished these from regular inspections.

Commission regulations governing the payment of aid to processors of skim-milk powder for livestock feed were challenged in a German federal court after a German milk producer was asked to pay for inspection costs on milk to be exported to Italy.
The producer asked whether treaty provisions against charges having the effect of customs duties would prohibit the exporter from having to bear the full costs of inspection under national law.
The court found systematic charges on goods to be exported did amount to a customs charge and prohibited such charges under treaty provisions protecting the free movement of goods.

"The abolition between member states of customs duties and charges having equivalent effect constitutes a fundamental principle of the common market...any exception must be strictly interpreted, must be clearly laid down," the court said.
"Aid for skimmed milk powder - Systematic inspections - Costs of inspections"
Bundesanstalt fur Landwirtschaft und Ernahrung and Deutsches Milch-Kontor GmbH
on the interpretation of Commission regulation 1624/76, 1725/79 and on the interpretation of articles 9,12,,16 and 95 of the EC Treaty

1. Article 2(1) and (4) of Commission regulation No 1624/76 concerning payment of aid for skimmed-milk powder denatured or processed in the territory of another member state, article 10 of Commission regulation 1725/79 on the rules for granting aid to skimmed-milk, in conjunction with article 34 of the EC treaty, preclude systematic inspections to verify compliance with the conditons as to the compositon and quality of skimmed-milk powder intended for processing into compound feedingstuffs in another member state on which entitlement to export refunds depends, where those inpsections are carried out, with a view to subsequent export of the goods inspected, inside the exporting state and not at the frontier. However, those provisions do not preclude such inspections if they are carried out only by means of spot checks.

2. A charge levied in respect of systematic inspections carried out inside the exporting state with a view to subsequent export of the goods inspected constitutes a charge having an effect equivalent to customs duties on exports, prohibited under articles 9 and 12 of the EC treaty, even if it corresponds to the actual cost of each inspection.
